sections.name: File setup, NotificationType
sections.title: Imports and notification type list
sections.what: Brings in icons and a style helper, and defines the seven allowed notification types. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: Fixes the set of categories so every notification is one of a known kind.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new type here also requires adding it to the lookup table below, or the card will use the fallback look.

sections.name: Notification
sections.title: Notification data shape
sections.what: Describes one notification: an id, a type, a title, a description, a time, an unread flag, and an optional priority.
sections.why: Sets the fields the card expects so the list passes the right data.
sections.watch_out: The priority field is optional and is not shown anywhere in this card.

sections.name: typeConfig
sections.title: Icon and color lookup table
sections.what: Maps each notification type to an icon, a text color, and a background color. Reminder uses a blue look, AI uses a violet look, upload uses the primary color, and alert, system and escalation use a red look.
sections.why: Makes each category recognizable at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The alert, system and escalation types share the same icon and colors, so users cannot tell them apart by look.

sections.name: NotificationCard
sections.title: Notification row layout
sections.what: Draws the row with the colored icon, the title, the time, a two-line description, an unread dot when relevant, and a menu icon that appears on hover. The whole row runs the click handler when pressed.
sections.why: Gives each notification a clear, tappable row that shows whether it is new.
sections.watch_out: The menu icon has no click action, so it looks usable but does nothing.

summary: A single notification row showing an icon, a title, a short description, a time, and an unread dot.
purpose: Displays one alert or message in the notification list, with color and icon chosen by its type.
why: A consistent card with a type-based look lets users tell reminders, uploads and alerts apart at a glance.
how: It looks up the type in a fixed table to pick an icon and colors, then draws the row. Unread items get a highlight and a dot. The whole row responds to a click, and a small menu icon appears on hover.
inputs: One notification with an id, type, title, description, time, unread flag, and optional priority, plus an optional click handler.
risks: The menu icon button does nothing when clicked. The priority field is accepted but never shown. An unknown type falls back to the generic info style.
debug: If a notification has the wrong icon, check its type value against the table. If the unread dot does not appear, check the unread flag.
